name: Manoah
description: Samson's father living before Israel's Monarchy

points: There was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah. He was married, but his wife was barren; she was not able to have any children.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: Manoah entreated the Lord: let the man of God which thou didst send come again unto us and teach us what we shall do unto the child that shall be born.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: The Most High hearkened to the voice of Manoah, and the angel of God came again unto the woman as she sat in the field; she made haste and ran and showed her husband that the man was back.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: Manoah arose and went after his wife, came to the man, and asked, art thou the man that spakest unto the woman? He said, I am.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: Manoah asked how they should order the child and what they should do unto him, and the angel reiterated the instructions he had already given: of all that I said unto the woman let her beware, and all that I commanded her let her observe while she carries this son.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: Manoah still did not know that he was an angel of the Lord.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: Manoah tried to detain the angel and make ready a kid for him, but the angel refused: though thou detain me, I will not eat of thy bread, and if thou wilt offer a burnt offering, thou must offer it unto the Lord.

The angel knew Manoah might try to offer it up to him, since he appeared like a god, so he directed the offering to the Lord. Israel is quick to worship anything that looks like it could be God because we cannot see the Most High, which is why the scriptures warn against the worshipping of angels.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: Manoah asked the angel his name, so that when his sayings came to pass they might do him honour.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: Manoah took a kid with a meat offering and offered it upon a rock unto the Lord, and the angel did wondrously: when the flame went up toward heaven from off the altar, the angel of the Lord ascended in the flame and went out of their sight.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: Manoah and his wife fell on their faces to the ground at the sight. This is the kind of thing Israel was able to see and witness with their own eyes.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: The angel appeared no more, and then Manoah knew that he was an angel of the Lord.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: Manoah said to his wife, we shall surely die, because we have seen God. This is a passage the contradictors point to, since the Bible says no man hath seen God; but God here is Elohim, which is plural and speaks of heavenly beings. They saw an angel, not the Most High God.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: His brethren and all the house of his father came down and took him, and brought him up and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the buryingplace of Manoah his father. And he judged Israel twenty years.

source.name: TIPNR, Translators Individualised Proper Names with all References, by Tyndale House Cambridge, STEPBible.org
